title: Swap a robot camera's frayed USB cable for the new one, plugged into the very port the old one came out of
instruction: The robot's camera cable (the one with the frayed jacket) is plugged into the USB hub. Swap it for the new cable parked in the grey dock. Hold the hub down with one hand while the other pulls the frayed cable's plug straight up out of its port, and drop it in the blue bin. Then take the new cable's plug out of the dock and push it all the way into the same port the frayed one came out of: the robot's software finds the camera by its port. Putting a plug into any other port, even part way, fails, and so does taking the new plug out of the dock before the frayed one is in the bin. Then take both arms back to where they started.
context: Robot data-collection rigs run several USB cameras through a hub, and their software finds each camera by the port it hangs off (its USB path), so a camera moved to another port comes up as the wrong one or not at all. Swapping a worn cable means remembering exactly which port it came out of, while holding the light hub down as the stiff plug comes out.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A white melamine desk riser, 17 cm deep, 40.5 cm wide and 6 cm high, from 23 to 40 cm forward and from 36 cm right to 4.5 cm left; its top is smooth and slick. (2) On it, a loose 7-port USB hub of dark grey ABS with silver trim, 31.6 by 5.6 by 2.4 cm on rubber feet (100 g), centred 25.8 cm forward and 8.8 cm right, its front face flush with the riser's front edge and its left end overhanging the riser by 2.5 cm. Its ports are on its top face in a row 3.6 cm apart, from 0.2 cm left to 21.4 cm right, each 20 by 11 mm and 17 mm deep (about 1.5 times real size) with a blue tongue and a blue light in front that is lit while a cable is in. (3) In four of the ports, right-angled USB-A plugs (a steel connector and a black overmould 22 by 12 by 30 mm) whose cables leave toward the front, run over the edge and down to the desk. One is the robot camera's black cable, its jacket split open for 12 mm next to the plug with the braid and wires showing; the other three are black, grey and white. Which port holds the camera's cable, and which three hold the others, depends on the trial's seed (140 layouts); with the default seed the camera's is the 1st port from the left (0.2 cm left) and the others are the 3rd, 4th and 6th. (4) The new cable's plug, the same kind, parked upright in a grey cable dock (5.6 by 4 cm, one socket) centred 25.8 cm forward and 30 cm right, its cable running down the riser's front like the others. (5) The robot computer's status box, black, 6 by 7 by 3.2 cm, on the riser's back corner 35.5 cm forward on the centre line, with a CAMERA lamp: green while the camera is plugged into its port, red otherwise. (6) A blue polypropylene bin on the desk, inside 16 by 16 cm with 3.5 cm walls, centred 12 cm forward and 19 cm right. Apart from the cables' ports, the layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Judged at the end, except "pulled out", "another port" and "too early", which count at any time. Pulled out: the frayed cable's plug came right out of the camera's port at some point. Another port: either plug sunk 5 mm or more into any port but the camera's. Too early: the new plug lifted 2 cm out of its dock while the frayed plug was not in the bin. 0.0 if another port or too early. 1.0: pulled out, the frayed plug lies in the blue bin, the new plug is pushed all the way into the camera's port (within 3 mm of its floor, held by the latch), and both arms are back where they started (each gripper's fingertip centre within 5 cm of its start); 0.5: pulled out, the frayed plug is in the bin and the new plug has caught in the camera's port; 0.25: pulled out; else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the hub and both plugs still.
reset_notes: Take the new plug out of the hub and park it back in the dock, and push the frayed cable's plug back into the camera's port for the trial's seed.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Simplified: a plug's latch is a joint along its port that holds it with about 3 N and lets it slide once pulled or pushed harder (stick-slip); a plug set on the camera port's mouth within 9 mm is drawn onto its axis. Ports are about 1.5 times real size; the cables are rigid and drop off the riser's front. The camera's port depends on the seed. Cameras 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).
